Definition: to butt with the horns; figuratively, to war against
BiblicalUsage: Nagach means to butt with the horns, and it is used for false prophets who promise victory with iron horns. In 1 Kings 22:11 Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah makes horns of iron and says, with these shalt thou push the Syrians until thou have consumed them, and in 2 Chronicles 18:10 the same words are spoken again before the king.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe iron horns make a good show and a bad prophecy; zedekiah pushed with horns he had made himself, and the battle went the other way.
RelatedEvents: Micaiah and Ahab's Death at Ramoth-Gilead
